correctness.rationale: A combinatorial window/qualifying-cluster count proves exact path tail contributions. Strict exchange inequalities prove uniqueness for positive minimal risk; all equality cases for zero risk are characterized. Direct polynomial comparisons prove the sole six-site crossover, with an all-sub-six combinatorial sharpness argument. Strict discrete convexity proves that balanced lengths minimize mean. The independent rational-edge-state verifier reproduced 2964 tail probabilities and checked 990 all-composition extrema, but finite checks are supplemental.

originality.rationale: New work is the all-n positive-risk fixed-edge-cycle threshold design and sharp six-vertex transmissibility-dependent worst intervention in contrast to mean optimization. Moore–Newman derive underlying percolation distributions; Enright–Meeks study worst-case deterministic edge deletion; Enns–Brandeau compare expected infection control algorithms; none of the inspected primary materials reports or entails the exact optimal gap configurations and crossover without further analysis. Related tree edge-blocking mean and path vertex-removal threshold results have different intervention domains. Priority remains provisional; unindexed literature is a risk.

value.rationale: The fixed-budget finite-ring cutoff produces a universal design rule when zero risk is unattainable. At the sharp six-site boundary, the intervention minimizing mean outbreak size becomes the unique worst intervention for crossing a three-infection threshold once transmission is high: a meaningful comparison of distinct public-health risk objectives, rather than an arbitrary coefficient or small numerical gain. Applies to idealized independent-edge transmission only.
